core.title: Collaborate through durable accountable delegation; mutate only under an assigned task
core.given: A workflow agent in the delegation chain operator → project main → named coordinator → driver works within its assigned project and task.
core.when: It delegates, messages, escalates, manages seats, inbox, merges or projections, or makes any code or repository mutation.
core.then: An existing assigned task in the same project must exist before any code or repository mutation; the task defines, assigns, executes, evidences and completes that work.
prefer: Proactively dispatch safe independent work; verify durable delivery and visible execution, distinguishing persisted, delivered, acknowledged, awaiting actor, executing.
Escalate material blockers upward with exact evidence, economical recommendation, viable alternatives and tradeoffs, and safe work that can continue.
Resolve assumptions or disagreement by time-boxed two-way evidence dialogue with the responsible actor; escalate only unresolved decisions.
Atomic assignment; unassigned work gets a project-main decision proposal: purpose, priority, recommended assignee, alternatives, consequences, dependencies, safe work meanwhile.
As a coordinating actor, reconcile the durable inbox as the first action at every session, turn and task resumption, and after every bounded action, phase completion or wait before the next action.
Promptly complete, supersede, reject or time-bound defer work; post decisions and open questions as messages when they happen.
Manage project-main, coordinator and driver seats only through the collaboration toolchain's canonical seat-lifecycle commands (the stack profile lists them).
Keep the full policy only in this convention; managed instruction-file blocks hold only its canonical pointer, and updating them preserves all user-authored content outside the marked block.
As operator, accept and receipt inbound communication from any seat.
avoid: Messages for anything but communication, evidence, consensus, authorization or status; requesting executable work in a message.
Inferring authorization; restarting productive sessions merely to relay policy.
Next-task discovery outside the same project; cross-project dialogue without a real dependency/interface or bypassing counterpart authority.
More than one bounded active task or worktree per driver; folding adjacent work in instead of assigning it separately.
Letting an actionable expects_result leave view before it is answered, executed, delegated with verified delivery and follow-up, or explicitly deferred, superseded or closed.
Operator sending substantive direction, results or wakes to any seat but the project main.
Anyone but the project main merging its repository; the operator may authorize, relay or inspect but never merges.
Hand-managing seats; skipping lifecycle steps or gates; duplicative or non-minimal implementations.
Dropping or rewriting user-authored content outside the marked block when updating a managed instruction-file block.
unless: A message may request executable work when it references an existing assigned task.
A seat may be started, stopped, rebound or succeeded by hand under explicit owner direction, completing the supported bind/reconciliation immediately after.
core.why: Accountable delegation, evidence-based escalation, economical delivery and bounded two-way resolution keep work durable, visible and within its assigned project and task.
evidence: Every commit/mutation maps to an existing assigned task in the same project, created/assigned before the mutation.
Message log shows only allowed message purposes and no executable-work requests lacking a reference to an existing assigned task.

Each driver has at most one active task and worktree at any time; next-task discovery stays in the same project; cross-project dialogue occurs only for a real dependency/interface via counterpart authority.

Merge log shows only the project main merging that project's repository; operator outbound substantive direction, results and wakes go only to the project main; every inbound communication to the operator has a receipt.
Coordinating actors' inbox reconciliation is the first action at each session/turn/task resumption and follows each bounded action, phase completion or wait before the next action.

Escalations contain exact evidence, recommendation, alternatives/tradeoffs and safe continuing work; escalated assumptions/disagreements follow a time-boxed dialogue and are unresolved; every actionable expects_result is still visible or has a permitted resolution state.
Seat lifecycle events come from the collaboration toolchain's canonical seat commands, or from owner-directed manual operations immediately followed by bind/reconciliation.
Managed instruction-file blocks contain only the canonical pointer; each managed projection update leaves content outside the marked block unchanged.
verification: Delivery states to distinguish: persisted, delivered, acknowledged, awaiting actor, executing.
expects_result resolution states: answered, executed, delegated (with verified delivery and follow-up), explicitly deferred, superseded, closed.
Allowed message purposes: communication, evidence, consensus, authorization, status.

Seat lifecycle events must originate from the collaboration toolchain's canonical seat-lifecycle commands; the stack profile lists them; owner-directed manual operations are accepted only when immediately followed by the supported bind/reconciliation (per unless).

Projection check: the full policy lives only in this convention; managed instruction-file blocks (per the stack profile) contain only its canonical pointer; the preservation check compares content outside the marked block before/after a managed projection update only.
Requires a lifecycle-event observer for coordinating actors (session, turn and task resumption, bounded-action, phase-completion and wait boundaries) to check inbox-reconciliation timing.
Requires a collaboration command/message log observer: who sent/receipted what to whom, which task it references, who merged, how seats were managed, and when managed projection blocks were updated.

Requires a diff/commit observer correlating each code or repository mutation with an existing assigned task in the same project created before the mutation, and comparing content outside the marked block before/after a managed projection update.
Escalation completeness, dialogue time-boxing, inferred authorization and delivery-state distinctions are llm_judged, not mechanically decidable.
Each doesNotFire exception is scoped to the single check that names it and exempts no other check of this rule.

Scope of the rule's activation is presence-based: work is in scope as soon as the delegated collaboration context identified by the profile is present (any single marker — a toolchain project or any delegation seat — suffices, so partial chains, a lone driver and owner-directed manual seat operations remain governed); only its total absence takes work out of scope.

fires: Any agent (including a single driver) makes a code or repository mutation before an assigned task for it exists.
A coordinator sends a message asking a driver to change code without referencing an existing assigned task.
A driver starts a second active task or worktree while one is still active, or folds adjacent work into its task.
An operator (not the project main) merges a project repository, or the operator sends substantive direction, results or wakes to a seat other than the project main.
The operator leaves inbound communication from a seat unaccepted or unreceipted.
A coordinating actor resumes a session, turn or task, or finishes a bounded action, phase or wait, and acts before reconciling its durable inbox.
A seat is started, stopped, rebound or succeeded by hand without explicit owner direction or without completing bind/reconciliation immediately after.
An actionable expects_result disappears from view without being answered, executed, delegated with verified delivery and follow-up, or explicitly deferred, superseded or closed.
A material blocker is escalated without exact evidence, an economical recommendation, viable alternatives and tradeoffs, and safe work that can continue.

An assumption or disagreement is escalated without first attempting time-boxed two-way evidence dialogue with the responsible actor, or a decision already resolved in that dialogue is escalated anyway.
Proactive next-task discovery looks for work in another project (no exception applies).
Cross-project dialogue happens without a real dependency or interface, or bypasses the counterpart project's authority.
A managed instruction-file projection update copies policy text into the block or alters user-authored content outside the marked block.
doesNotFire: Work in a context with no delegated collaboration context of the kind the profile identifies: none of the delegation seats (operator, project main, coordinator or driver) and no project of the collaboration toolchain is present. Any single marker — including a lone driver seat — keeps work in scope, and owner-directed manual seat operations remain governed (seat-management exception).

For the message-purpose check only: a message carrying status, evidence, consensus, authorization or communication that requests no executable work (other duties such as delivery verification still apply).
For the message-purpose check only: a message requesting work that references an existing assigned task.
For the cross-project dialogue check only (not next-task discovery): dialogue about a real dependency or interface conducted through the counterpart project's authority.
For the seat-management check only: manual seat start/stop/rebind/succession under explicit owner direction followed immediately by the supported bind/reconciliation.

For the projection check only: edits to managed instruction-file content outside the managed block that are not part of a managed projection update (they remain subject to the assigned-task requirement).

profileRequirements.meaning: What identifies the delegated collaboration context: presence of the collaboration toolchain's project or any of its delegation seats. Any single marker suffices — a partial chain, including a lone driver, is governed, and command-managed seats are NOT a prerequisite (owner-directed manual seat operations stay governed). The core's out-of-scope exception (activation.doesNotFire[0]) refers to this entry; only the absence of every marker takes work out of scope.
profileRequirements.bunValue: an atdd-flow project or any operator/main/coordinator/driver seat (any one marker suffices; partial chains, a single driver and owner-directed manual seat operations remain governed)

profileRequirements.meaning: The canonical seat-lifecycle commands of the stack's collaboration toolchain, which alone may manage project-main, coordinator and driver seats; the seat-management check and the seat-command evidence are evaluated against this list.
profileRequirements.bunValue: spawn, bind, pi runtime launch, task lifecycle, handover

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete address of the project's main seat, substituted wherever the core refers to it neutrally as 'the project main' (operator routing of direction, results and wakes; merge authority; merge-log evidence).
The name patterns of the instruction files that carry managed projection blocks of this policy, targeted by the file_kind activation fact and the projection checks.

proposedKeys.meaning: How the delegated collaboration context is recognized in the stack: presence of the collaboration toolchain's project or ANY of its delegation seats places work inside the delegation chain that collaboration rules govern. Any single marker suffices — a partial chain, including a lone driver, is governed — and command-managed seats are not a prerequisite (owner-directed manual seat operations stay governed); absence of every marker takes the work out of scope.
proposedKeys.bunValue: an atdd-flow project or any operator/main/coordinator/driver seat (any one marker suffices; partial chains, a single driver and owner-directed manual seat operations remain governed)
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No existing key names the workflow collaboration context: roles, layout, suffix, urn and idiom describe code and artifact structure, enforcement describes check running, and tooling covers package/test/URN tooling only. The toolchain-and-project binding that scopes collaboration rules to a delegated context has no slot; tooling.seat_commands lists commands but does not identify the delegated-project context.

proposedKeys.meaning: The collaboration toolchain's canonical commands for seat lifecycle and handover, through which project-main, coordinator and driver seats must be managed.
proposedKeys.bunValue: spawn, bind, pi runtime launch, task lifecycle, handover
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The tooling group covers package manager, test runner and URN resolver only; no existing key names the workflow toolchain's seat-management commands, and idiom.* describes code constructs, not workflow commands.

proposedKeys.meaning: The concrete seat-address idiom by which the collaboration toolchain names the project's main seat, substituted wherever a core refers to it neutrally as 'the project main' (operator routing of direction, results and wakes; merge authority; merge-log evidence).
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The idiom group binds neutral concepts to concrete constructs, but every existing key describes code constructs (handlers, guards, mappers, request/gate markup); none names a workflow-seat address, and the workflow keys proposed so far (tooling.delegation_context, tooling.seat_commands) identify context and commands, not the address form of the project-main seat.

proposedKeys.meaning: Name patterns of the agent-instruction file kind: the files that carry managed projection blocks of the collaboration policy.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: suffix.<file_kind>'s closed parameter list (source, unit_test, acceptance_test, e2e_test, markup, plan_artifact, config) has no kind for agent-instruction files, and no other group names these files.

neutralityNotes: The delegation chain (operator → project main → named coordinator → driver), seats, durable inbox, expects_result, worktree and the delivery-state ladder are this convention's own workflow model and stay in the core essentially verbatim. Realization-specific content is carried elsewhere, not dropped: the seat-address syntax main@project (profile key idiom.project_main_address; the core says 'the project main' and the profile binds the concrete address); the atdd-flow toolchain name (bunOnly); the canonical seat-command list including 'pi runtime launch' (proposed profile key tooling.seat_commands) and the managed instruction-file names AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md (proposed profile key suffix.agent_instruction), because the closed vocabulary has no fitting key for either. The rule's scope restriction is presence-based in both realizations: doesNotFire[0]'s 'no atdd-flow delegation' is expressed as the absence of every marker of the delegated collaboration context identified by proposed profile key tooling.delegation_context, whose Bun value mirrors the original any-marker semantics (an atdd-flow project or any operator/main/coordinator/driver seat). Partial delegation chains, a single driver (fires[0] keeps 'including a single driver') and owner-directed manual seat operations remain in scope in the core exactly as in Bun; command-managed seats are an obligation on seat handling (prefer[6], unless[1]), never a scope prerequisite. Activation-fact notes (observer descriptions, judging needs, 'files carrying managed projection blocks') moved into core.verification since the neutral fact shape carries only fact/values/observability; the fact path_glob was renamed to the closed enum value file_kind. No exception or condition was dropped or added: unless, the check-scoped doesNotFire items and all prefer/avoid/evidence obligations are preserved one-to-one. audit, splitSuggestion (whose sub-obligations all remain in prefer/avoid/unless/evidence), sharedNodes, additions and trace are realization bookkeeping rather than agent-facing items, so they are not classified.
